evals.prompt: We have 140 call sites across the billing and quotes services still importing the deprecated `moment` date library, and security wants it gone before the Q3 audit freeze next Friday because of a transitive CVE. Figure it out and replace every call site with `date-fns`, keeping the formatting output byte-for-byte identical where it feeds the PDF invoice renderer. I want this landed as a stack I can review commit by commit.
evals.expected_output: The response opens with Phase A framing before touching any code: a falsifiable definition of done (e.g. zero remaining moment imports, build green, PDF invoice output byte-identical to a captured baseline), the scope quantified as 140 call sites across billing and quotes, and a rigor level pushed high because of the CVE deadline and the one-way-door risk of silently changing invoice output. Phase B follows with a verification harness (a script that diffs rendered PDFs against baseline output) built and a baseline captured before any call site is migrated, then the work decomposed into independently-landable units sequenced riskiest-unknown-first. It must not start editing call sites before that phase list is presented.
expectations: States a falsifiable definition of done, e.g. all 140 call sites migrated with zero remaining moment imports and byte-identical PDF output, not a vague quality bar
Quantifies scope explicitly as 140 call sites across the billing and quotes services
Names a rigor level and ties it explicitly to the CVE deadline and/or the blast radius of changing invoice output
Describes capturing a baseline of current PDF output and building a diff-based verification harness before migrating any call site
Decomposes the migration into independently-landable units sequenced riskiest-unknown-first rather than one giant edit
Does not begin editing or migrating any call site before the phase list is presented
Does not state the verification harness is built after the migration work rather than before it

evals.prompt: hey figure it out, i'm heading to bed. we need tenant-scoped rate limiting across the api gateway plus the 3 downstream worker services, with a fallback to a local in-memory limiter when the primary redis store is unreachable. build it out, i'll review the whole trail when i wake up around 7am, don't wait on me for anything reversible.
evals.expected_output: The response states a falsifiable definition of done up front (e.g. requests over the per-tenant threshold are rejected across the gateway and all 3 workers, and the redis-down path is exercised and falls back correctly) and quantifies scope as the gateway plus 3 worker services plus the fallback path. It proceeds without waiting for a checkpoint since the work is reversible, and it explicitly plans a running decision-trail log (per the show-me-your-work skill) rather than a summary written only at the end, so the log is there to review at 7am. It must not pause with a clarifying question on a reversible design choice and must not defer the verification harness until after the limiter is implemented.
expectations: States a falsifiable definition of done for the rate limiter and its redis-down fallback before starting implementation
Quantifies scope as the api gateway plus the 3 downstream worker services plus the fallback path
Proceeds without asking the human to confirm a reversible design choice, citing that the work is reversible and the human is stepping away
Explicitly plans a decision-trail log written as the work proceeds rather than assembled only at the end
Notes the trail is meant to be read after the human returns, so it can be audited without them present
Does not ask a blocking clarifying question about a reversible implementation detail before proceeding
Does not describe building or exercising the verification harness only after the limiter code is written

evals.prompt: figure it out: /checkout 500s whenever the cart has more than 20 items. fix it.
evals.expected_output: The response recognizes this as a single reported defect on one endpoint, not a large or cross-cutting change, and states that it routes to the Bug fix playbook instead of designing a bespoke figure-it-out workflow. It gives a one-line reason (a focused single-unit defect matches an existing playbook) rather than producing a Phase A through E plan, and it does not start editing checkout code before naming that routing decision.
expectations: Explicitly identifies the task as a single focused bug fix rather than a large or cross-cutting change
States that the task routes to the Bug fix playbook instead of a bespoke figure-it-out workflow
Gives a concrete reason for the routing, e.g. single endpoint / single defect, not ambitious or multi-part
Does not produce a Phase A through E bespoke phase list for this task
Does not start editing the checkout code before stating the routing decision
Does not invent a falsifiable definition-of-done framing as if this were a figure-it-out run rather than a Bug fix
